output.headline: Sponsor with a same-sub-sector precedent and upper-quartile pricing, but a thin Midwest record and smaller typical deal make it a lower-priority call.
output.differentiator: Pays a median 15.7x, above Advent and GTCR on the priority list. Its Quality Medical Group precedent ($187M) is in the target's own sub-sector and close to its size. [V:comps, D:MA-2022-0350]
output.why_them: Pays above upper-quartile comps; adjacent provider record; lower-priority call

acquirer_overview.title: Large sponsor with a half-provider record since 2016
points: Financial sponsor with $303.0 billion in assets under management as of December 31, 2025 [P:1].
18 deals from 2016 to 2023; 15 closed, and 17 of 18 were control deals [K:closed_share, K:control_share, T:record].
Provider services made up 9 of 18 deals; its home sub-sector is Health Insurance, and it has no open platform [A:angles, B:buyer].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Growth appetite and a same-sub-sector deal, offset by weak Midwest fit
points: Growth was a motive in 10 of 18 deals, matching the target's 11.0% revenue growth [M:high_growth, X:target].
Has bought from this kind of seller (a modest factor), with 1 deal in the target's sub-sector and 8 in adjacent provider sub-sectors [S:own_fit_s, T:record].
Past buying in this or a neighbouring region is a slight factor against; only 1 deal was in the Midwest [S:geo_fit, T:record].

precedent_activity.title: Closest precedent is a $187M same-sub-sector deal, but a minority stake
points: Quality Medical Group: $187M minority investment, 2022, at 11.2x EV/EBITDA, in the target's own sub-sector [D:MA-2022-0350].
Granite Dental Network: $203M platform investment, 2021, at 12.2x, an adjacent provider sub-sector deal in the target's size band [D:MA-2021-0439].
Only Midwest deal: Metro Medical Associates, $15M, 2018, at 8.8x, far below the target's size [D:MA-2018-0415].

valuation_context.title: 75th percentile pricing is defensible and within TPG's own pricing range
points: 70 comparable deals: 10.7x at the lower quartile, 12.8x median, 15.3x at the 75th percentile [V:comps].
Target margin of 16.8% against a comparable median of 12.9% supports the 75th percentile [V:comps].
TPG's median paid is 15.7x; IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target, on a $128M equity cheque [V:comps, V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Size stretch
risk_flags.concern: Median deal of $88M is under half the target's $200M EV [T:record].
risk_flags.mitigant: 8 of 18 deals sit in the $100M-$400M band; the biggest was $1,388M [K:size_band, T:record].
risk_flags.reality: Capacity exists, but this is a larger-than-typical cheque for TPG [T:record, C:conviction].

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below the 20% target [V:lbo].
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M [V:lbo].
risk_flags.reality: At the same exit the maximum is $193M, below $200M; the bid needs a platform exit [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Thin Midwest record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal in the target region, and geography is a signal against [T:record, S:geo_fit].
risk_flags.mitigant: Growth and adjacent provider buying are signals for; one Midwest deal exists [S:activity, S:sector_rel, D:MA-2018-0415].
risk_flags.reality: Welsh Carson and GTCR have far deeper Midwest records on the priority list, a stronger regional claim [T:record].

conviction.rationale: Ranked 9th on the priority list of 10, with a likelihood of 3.7%. The record is relevant (1 own-sub-sector and 8 adjacent provider deals), but the $88M median deal is under half the $200M EV. [R:rank, C:conviction]
